content.title: About
content.content: Cooked green pepper is the mature fruit of the sweet pepper plant (Capsicum annuum) that, after heat treatment, retains a bright color, tender texture, and a mildly sweet flavor. It is commonly used as an ingredient in soups, stews, salads, and side dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green peppers are harvested before full ripening, making them less sweet than red or yellow peppers.
Cooking increases the bioavailability of certain antioxidants such as vitamin C and carotenoids.
In cuisine, cooked green pepper is often used for stuffed peppers and sauces.
Different regions have their own names: in the US it’s called "green bell pepper", in Spain "pimiento verde".

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Cooked green pepper retains a high amount of vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and flavonoids help combat free radicals, reducing the risk of chronic diseases.

items.title: Low‑calorie source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety while the pepper remains low in calories.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamins B6 and folate are involved in protein metabolism and DNA synthesis.

items.title: Supports heart health
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure, contributing to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to pepper, manifested as skin rash or swelling.

items.title: Food interactions
items.content: Large amounts of pepper may affect the action of certain medications, such as anticoagulants, due to its vitamin K content.

items.title: Sodium excess
items.content: If the pepper is prepared with added salt, total sodium intake should be monitored.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked green pepper can be added to soups, stews, pasta, salads, used as a filling for stuffed vegetables, or served as a side dish. It is convenient to dice or slice it.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked green pepper in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags.
